_pipeline_state: Rules in force: modality-from-structure (1b, modality.py), assay attribution (6), within-structure druggability (4.0/4a — volume the reported computed number, druggability never load-bearing), pocket_scan chains/site_residues (2b), rule 13 nulls (affinity/cofold/patents/OpenTargets), rule 14/15 count reconciliation. pocket_scan run via the DEPLOYED Modal app druggability-pocket-scan (fpocket 4.2.3 + P2Rank 2.5.1 + mdpocket, D swept {1.6,2.4}); Paperclip proteins (uniprot_v/pdb_v/chembl_v + raw chembl.*); metapredict disorder; Foldseek (proto_tools, public server).
_headline: The druggable ENTITY here is gamma-secretase, a DIFFERENT protein, not a pocket on NOTCH3. Every small-molecule 'active' at this accession is gamma-secretase-inhibitor chemistry read out through a Notch intracellular-domain cleavage reporter or undefined patent boilerplate; the top compound is equipotent (1.0 nM) on NOTCH1 and NOTCH3 via identical reporters. No ChEMBL assay measures binding to a NOTCH3 pocket; all 6 PDB structures are apo. Tractable-looking chemistry, poor selectivity, wrong target.

input.interaction_to_disrupt: Notch3 signalling via gamma-secretase cleavage of the receptor
input._disease_context_reasoning: Left null per 'null if unclear — don't invent'. The retrieved small-molecule/clinical precedent is oncology (anti-NOTCH2/3 antibody tarextumab in pancreatic/SCLC; gamma-secretase-inhibitor chemistry), which does not cleanly match a stromal/vascular context (NOTCH3's Mendelian disease CADASIL), so the evidence does not settle a single disease context and none is invented.
input._mechanism_hypothesis_reasoning: 'unknown' is the least-wrong enum because this is NOT a NOTCH3-pocket question at all. Disrupting 'Notch3 signalling via gamma-secretase cleavage' with a small molecule means inhibiting gamma-secretase (a separate multi-subunit intramembrane protease), not binding an orthosteric/allosteric/oligomer site on NOTCH3. orthosteric/allosteric/oligomer_destabilisation all presuppose a NOTCH3 pocket that the retrieved chemistry never engages; 'unknown' records that the site is not on NOTCH3.

axis_conflict: The retrieved-precedent axis LOOKS tractable (57 distinct small molecules, best 1.0 nM IC50) but collapses on attribution: 62.7% of activity is patent boilerplate ('pharmacological properties of the compounds of this invention', assay 1641354, no defined molecular mechanism) and 33.9% is a NICD3 cellular reporter ('Inhibition of Notch3 intracellular domain fragment transfected in HeLa', assay 1468308) — a readout of gamma-secretase cleavage, not binding to a NOTCH3 pocket. The single best-potency compound (CHEMBL3410169) is equipotent 1.0 nM on NOTCH1 AND NOTCH3 via identical intracellular-domain reporters, the signature of a pan-Notch gamma-secretase inhibitor. The computed axis independently finds all 6 PDB structures apo (heteroatoms only Ca2+, NAG glycan, glycerol/acetate/EDO/chloride) and no anchorable small-molecule site on the NRR. The two axes agree that NOTCH3-direct small-molecule tractability is NOT established; they disagree only in that a naive read of the precedent count would call it tractable. The druggable entity implied by the interaction is gamma-secretase, a different protein.

The most advanced agent directly targeting NOTCH3 is TAREXTUMAB (OMP-59R5), an anti-NOTCH2/3 monoclonal antibody (chembl.molecule_dictionary.molecule_type = 'Antibody') that reached Phase 2 and was not advanced — a clinical biologic, not approved, and biologic engagement of the NRR epitope is target validation, NOT evidence of small-molecule tractability. tractability._primary: No small-molecule site could be anchored on NOTCH3, so the computed axis reports NO site quantity. site_hypothesis_basis = not_established. This is honest, not a null-with-no-reason: there is no holo ligand, no partner structure for the (enzymatic, gamma-secretase) interaction, and the scanned region is an extracellular autoinhibitory domain, not the intramembrane cleavage machinery. Documentary geometry is in the caveat.

pocket_volume_a3._documentary: Not reported as a site volume because no site was established. For the record, fpocket on the apo NRR found 15-24 pockets per structure at D=1.6 (largest 293-514 A^3) merging above 1000 A^3 at D=2.4; mdpocket's persistent cavity (site_from_density) measured 465-704 A^3 across the 4 structures but is ligand-UNANCHORED (no holo donor), so its identity is unverified (rule 4b) and it is not adopted as the site.

pocket_druggability._comparability: Not reported: no site was anchored, so any pocket rank would be max_druggability_no_ligand_site ('most druggable pocket anywhere'), which rule 4.0 bans as a reportable value. fpocket druggability is a within-structure quantity and carries no verdict here.
pocket_druggability._false_negative_rate: Not applicable — no druggability value is reported. In general a large fraction of pockets with a drug physically bound score below 0.1 (e.g. EGFR 6LUD with osimertinib 0.013; JAK1 median 0.009 across nine approved drugs), so a low druggability is never evidence against a site; the demoted number carries no negative verdict (rule 4.0/4a).

cryptic_evidence._note: Vajda 2018 census the cryptic call would rest on.
cryptic_evidence.basis: All 6 PDB structures are apo (no drug-like ligand). No holo reference exists, so backbone C-alpha displacement at any candidate site cannot be measured and geometric scoring is blind to cryptic sites (CLAUDE.md rules 3 and 5); cryptic_pocket_risk is therefore high but the cryptic call itself (is_cryptic) is not made.
cryptic_evidence.definition: Vajda et al. 2018: cryptic only if the site is absent in all/nearly all unbound structures — not assessable here without a holo reference (CryptoBench pocket-residue RMSD > 2 A apo-vs-holo cannot be computed with no holo).

pocket_vs_interface._note: The interaction to disrupt is an enzymatic cleavage performed by gamma-secretase, a different protein; there is no NOTCH3+gamma-secretase complex structure to classify a pocket against. interface stage was not_run (no partner_structures).

tractability.caveat: The interaction named ('Notch3 signalling via gamma-secretase cleavage') is disrupted by a small molecule only at GAMMA-SECRETASE, a separate multi-subunit intramembrane protease — not at a pocket on NOTCH3. The pocket scan (deployed Modal app druggability-pocket-scan; fpocket 4.2.3 + P2Rank 2.5.1 + mdpocket) ran on the apo NRR ensemble 4ZLP/5CZV/5CZX/6XSW (chains resolved by accession; in 5CZX chain A is the NRR and Fab chains H/L are present, L flagged as a polymer-ligand contributing 50% of one pocket's lining). It found real cavities (15-24 pockets/structure at D=1.6, largest 293-514 A^3; merged >1000 A^3 at D=2.4; mdpocket persistent cavity 465-704 A^3) but NONE could be anchored to a small-molecule site: there is no holo ligand, no partner complex for the enzymatic interaction, and the only mdpocket site is a ligand-unanchored persistence cavity of unverified identity. Volume and druggability are therefore not reported as site quantities (site_hypothesis_basis = not_established). All structures are apo, so cryptic risk is high and geometric scoring is blind (rule 3). Full-length disorder is 25.8% (metapredict); the region just C-terminal to the NRR (1628-1816, juxtamembrane) is disordered. Reading any of these geometric numbers as a NOTCH3 druggability verdict would be a category error: the chemistry that exists targets gamma-secretase.

checks_run: 1. Does the actives count collapse to one assay? (assay-description GROUP BY)
2. Is the best potency from a characterised assay?
2b. Cross-accession check on the top compound

findings: 1 FIRED: one assay (1641354, patent boilerplate 'pharmacological properties of the compounds of this invention') is 62.7% of activity; the NICD3 reporter (1468308) is 33.9%. The count is about these two assays, not about NOTCH3.
2 FIRED: best potency 1.0 nM comes from a NICD3 cellular cleavage reporter (assay 1468308), not a characterised NOTCH3-binding assay. best_potency_characterised=false.

2b FIRED (highest-yield): CHEMBL3410169 is 1.0 nM IC50 on BOTH NOTCH1 (P46531) and NOTCH3 (Q9UM47) via identical 'Inhibition of NotchN intracellular domain fragment' reporters. The measured potency belongs to gamma-secretase (which cleaves all Notch receptors), not to NOTCH3 selectively. This is 'readout protein is not the measured protein' plus pan-family off-target in one compound.
2c CLEAN: no approved-drug rows are being counted as NOTCH3 binders (approved_small_molecules is empty; the one clinical small molecule, varegacestat, is flagged as a gamma-secretase inhibitor).
3 FIRED (partly): the 57 compounds are one chemotype family (benzodiazepine/dibenzazepine-dipeptide gamma-secretase inhibitors) from patent-scale SAR across two assays; not independent programmes.
4 CLEAN and decisive: no holo ligand exists to be drug-like or a frequent hitter — all 6 structures are apo (only Ca2+, NAG, glycerol, acetate, EDO, chloride). Zero drug-like co-crystals.
5 / 5a CLEAN: no druggability value is reported and none is read as a finding; no site was anchored (site_hypothesis_basis not_established), so there is no across-structure spread to over-interpret.

6 FIRED: this accession carries TWO ChEMBL targets — the NOTCH3 single protein (tid 109578) and a pan-Notch FAMILY target (tid 119724, n_target_components=4). Activity on the family target is inherited across NOTCH1-4, not measured on NOTCH3.

7 FIRED: TAREXTUMAB (anti-NOTCH2/3 antibody) reached Phase 2 (pancreatic Cancer Med 2019;8:5148-57; solid-tumour Invest New Drugs 2019;37:722-730) and was not advanced. The gamma-secretase-inhibitor CLASS is limited by on-target pan-Notch toxicity: GSIs cause intestinal goblet-cell metaplasia (Milano et al., Toxicol Sci 2004) and GI toxicity has driven trial design for even 'selective' GSIs (PF-03084014, Wei et al., Mol Cancer Ther) — the direct clinical consequence of the poor selectivity this dossier surfaces.

8 CLEAN/RELEVANT: the look-alike check is central here — VAREGACESTAT and all 57 'NOTCH3 actives' are gamma-secretase inhibitors, not NOTCH3 binders; they are correctly kept out of any NOTCH3-direct tractability claim.
9 did not fire: every claim was settleable inside the pipeline (ChEMBL targets, assay descriptions, cross-accession); no upstream-graph ask issued.
10/10b/11 did not fire: the dossier leans on no separation, threshold or negative boundary.
falsification._survived_note: The claim 'NOTCH3 is small-molecule tractable (57 nM-potent actives)' does NOT survive: checks 1, 2, 2b, 3 and 6 show the actives measure gamma-secretase cleavage across the whole Notch family, not binding to a NOTCH3 pocket. What survives is a correct negative/insufficient reading — the chemistry is real but its target is gamma-secretase.

next_experiment.description: Two experiments. (1) Test whether any small molecule binds a NOTCH3 pocket DIRECTLY: SPR/ITC or a fragment/biophysical screen against the isolated NRR (UniProt 1378-1640) and against the intracellular ANK domain. (2) Confirm the mechanism of the ~1 nM cellular actives is gamma-secretase inhibition: a biochemical gamma-secretase cleavage assay plus a counter-screen of the top compounds across NOTCH1-4 and non-Notch substrates (e.g. APP), to quantify the pan-Notch/APP selectivity liability.
next_experiment.rationale: All 57 reported actives derive from a pan-Notch/NICD cellular cleavage reporter or undefined patent boilerplate, and the top compound is equipotent (1.0 nM) on NOTCH1 and NOTCH3 via identical intracellular-domain reporters — the signature of a gamma-secretase inhibitor. No ChEMBL assay measures binding to a NOTCH3 pocket, and all 6 crystal structures are apo, so the geometric axis cannot anchor a site. Whether NOTCH3 itself is small-molecule bindable is therefore genuinely unmeasured.
next_experiment.resolves: Whether NOTCH3 (as opposed to gamma-secretase) presents a druggable small-molecule pocket at all, and whether any of the existing chemistry has a NOTCH3-selective binding component rather than being purely gamma-secretase inhibition acting on the whole Notch family.

limitations.message: No small-molecule site could be anchored on the apo NRR ensemble (site_hypothesis_basis not_established): no holo ligand, no partner complex for the enzymatic interaction, and the only mdpocket site is a ligand-unanchored persistence cavity of unverified identity (rule 4b). Documentary geometry is in tractability.pocket_volume_a3._documentary; it is not reported as a site volume.
No site anchored, so any druggability would be max_druggability_no_ligand_site, which rule 4.0 bans as a reportable value. Not reported.
No anchored site to characterise; not reported.
No small-molecule site established to compare against annotated features.
No holo ligand site exists to compute a Jaccard against (all apo).
Cryptic displacement is measured apo-vs-holo; no holo reference exists (all 6 apo), so it cannot be computed (cryptic_status not_run).
No site to score for a consensus fraction; only ensemble denominators (n_structures 4, n_measurements 8) are recorded.

The interaction named ('Notch3 signalling via gamma-secretase cleavage') is disrupted by a small molecule only at GAMMA-SECRETASE, a separate multi-subunit intramembrane protease — not at a pocket on NOTCH3. The pocket scan (deployed Modal app druggability-pocket-scan; fpocket 4.2.3 + P2Rank 2.5.1 + mdpocket) ran on the apo NRR ensemble 4ZLP/5CZV/5CZX/6XSW (chains resolved by accession; in 5CZX chain A is the NRR and Fab chains H/L are present, L flagged as a polymer-ligand contributing 50% of one pocket's lining). It found real cavities (15-24 pockets/structure at D=1.6, largest 293-514 A^3; merged >1000 A^3 at D=2.4; mdpocket persistent cavity 465-704 A^3) but NONE could be anchored to a small-molecule site: there is no holo ligand, no partner complex for the enzymatic interaction, and the only mdpocket site is a ligand-unanchored persistence cavity of unverified identity. Volume and druggability are therefore not reported as site quantities (site_hypothesis_basis = not_established). All structures are apo, so cryptic risk is high and geometric scoring is blind (rule 3). Full-length disorder is 25.8% (metapredict); the region just C-terminal to the NRR (1628-1816, juxtamembrane) is disordered. Reading any of these geometric numbers as a NOTCH3 druggability verdict would be a category error: the chemistry that exists targets gamma-secretase.
Metric metric.disorder_fraction carries no evidence or assumption link.

counterfactuals.change: Two experiments. (1) Test whether any small molecule binds a NOTCH3 pocket DIRECTLY: SPR/ITC or a fragment/biophysical screen against the isolated NRR (UniProt 1378-1640) and against the intracellular ANK domain. (2) Confirm the mechanism of the ~1 nM cellular actives is gamma-secretase inhibition: a biochemical gamma-secretase cleavage assay plus a counter-screen of the top compounds across NOTCH1-4 and non-Notch substrates (e.g. APP), to quantify the pan-Notch/APP selectivity liability.
counterfactuals.result: Whether NOTCH3 (as opposed to gamma-secretase) presents a druggable small-molecule pocket at all, and whether any of the existing chemistry has a NOTCH3-selective binding component rather than being purely gamma-secretase inhibition acting on the whole Notch family.
counterfactuals.meaning: All 57 reported actives derive from a pan-Notch/NICD cellular cleavage reporter or undefined patent boilerplate, and the top compound is equipotent (1.0 nM) on NOTCH1 and NOTCH3 via identical intracellular-domain reporters — the signature of a gamma-secretase inhibitor. No ChEMBL assay measures binding to a NOTCH3 pocket, and all 6 crystal structures are apo, so the geometric axis cannot anchor a site. Whether NOTCH3 itself is small-molecule bindable is therefore genuinely unmeasured.
